title: Validate JDK lane runtime or toolchain alignment
outOfScope: Adopter Maven or Gradle build files, module selection, toolchain installation or switching, JAVA_HOME mutation, private repository settings and credentials, hosted CI configuration, release publication, and the generic project-quality contract.

sources.reason: Authoritative requirement: Java lane selection must validate the actual runtime or declared toolchain and fail closed on a mismatch.
Current installed Java stack preset delegates its project commands without runtime-major validation.
Canonical public configuration boundary says adopters retain their own JDK choice and must calibrate it.
Installer distribution glob ships ai_ helper scripts and Java stack preset files to adopters.
Distribution regression surface for installed runtime helpers.

riskAssessment.reason: A false match would let an adopter run a Java 8/17 lane on Java 21, while an over-broad check could attempt to manage the adopter toolchain. The implementation must only observe the selected runtime and block missing or mismatched facts.
riskAssessment.unknownsReviewReason: The exact adopter command, module path, and runtime manager are intentionally project-owned configuration; this Work Item defines only a portable validation interface.

reasons: The change adds a fail-closed installed-stack validation boundary and focused regression coverage.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized automatic execution of the complete remediation plan and requested that this authority be recorded in every Work Item Contract; no gate bypass is authorized.

preReviewWarnings: Verify that validation observes the exact runtime selected by JAVA_HOME or PATH and never installs, switches, or silently substitutes an adopter JDK.
Verify that missing required-major configuration and invalid/mismatched runtime produce actionable blocked recovery messages.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: The installed Java preset accepts a declared lane identifier and required Java major, then verifies the Java executable selected by the declared JAVA_HOME or PATH before every project quality command.

A missing required Java major, missing executable, unparsable runtime version, or runtime-major mismatch fails closed with a lane-specific recovery message and never executes the delegated project command.
A matching legacy Java version string and a matching modern Java version string permit the delegated command, while a mismatched command is rejected by focused regression tests.

The installer distributes the runtime validator to an adopter, and English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese Java configuration guidance describe only observation and recovery—not toolchain installation, switching, or private configuration.
guidelines: The validator must use only Python standard-library process and text parsing APIs so the installed template has no new runtime dependency.
Public configuration names, failure semantics, and recovery guidance must be documented consistently in English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese.
Do not change the adopter's Java executable, JAVA_HOME, Maven/Gradle command, module path, credentials, or toolchain manager.

intent.problem: Selecting a Java lane can currently change only a project command or module path; it does not prove that the Maven or Gradle process will run on the lane's required Java major. An adopter using Java 21 can therefore label a command as a Java 8 lane and get an unsafe, misleading execution.
constraints: Keep the validation portable and dependency-free for installation into adopter repositories.
Observe the executable selected by the declared JAVA_HOME or PATH; never install, switch, mutate, or infer a toolchain.
Block before every delegated Java quality command when configuration is absent or the actual Java major does not match.
Keep module selection, Maven settings, private repository access, credentials, hosted CI, and release work outside this Work Item.
intent.rationale: A small explicit configuration contract couples the declared lane to the runtime that will actually execute the command, restoring trustworthy Java-lane evidence without taking control of adopter environments.

rawUserRequest: Execute the complete remediation plan automatically; record authorization in every Work Item Contract. For #620, validate JDK lane against the actual Java runtime or verified toolchain and fail closed with recovery guidance on mismatch. Do not use temporary workarounds or omit related documentation.

declaredIntent.summary: Make Java lane evidence trustworthy by checking the actual selected Java runtime against an adopter-declared required major before project quality commands execute.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A Java lane declares major 8 and the selected executable reports legacy Java version 1.8.0_*.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The validator identifies major 8 and permits the delegated project command.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add a subprocess-based unit test with a fake executable reporting 1.8.0_*, then assert success and delegated-command permission.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A lane declares major 17 but the executable selected through JAVA_HOME or PATH reports Java 21.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The validator returns a blocked mismatch diagnostic before the delegated command runs.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add focused tests for both explicit runtime selection and mismatch output.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The preset omits required-major configuration or points to a missing/unparseable Java executable.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The preset fails closed with the missing fact and recovery condition; it never selects or installs a toolchain.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Test missing configuration, missing executable, and unparsable version cases; assert the recovery text and nonzero result.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: An adopter installs the Java preset and reads its configuration guidance.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The validator is present in the distribution and the three language variants preserve the observation-only boundary.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Extend installer and documentation metadata regressions to assert the shipped helper and canonical configuration markers.
